description: Most of the work is managing a chain of parties who can each kill the deal, and entitlement takes longer than construction. Do not make market predictions the centerpiece.

questions.text: How many people can kill a deal, and which one usually does?
questions.lands_because: Frames the job as chain management rather than salesmanship, which is accurate and immediately signals you understand the work.
followups: Tell me about one that died at the eleventh hour.

questions.text: How long does the paperwork take compared to the building?
questions.lands_because: Entitlement, zoning, financing, and approvals routinely dwarf construction timelines, and almost nobody outside the industry knows that.
followups: What is the single longest thing you have waited on?

questions.text: What do you know about a property in the first five minutes that the listing will never say?
questions.lands_because: Rapid assessment is real expertise here - drainage, orientation, deferred maintenance, the neighbors - and it makes great concrete audio.
followups: What do buyers fixate on that does not matter?

questions.text: Whose interests are you actually representing, and does the client understand that?
questions.lands_because: Agency, dual agency, and commission incentives are structurally confusing to consumers, and a straight answer here is a real public service.
followups: How does the commission structure pull on that?

questions.text: What have you built or sold that you would not want to live in or next to?
questions.lands_because: Personal-stake framing gets past the standard defense of the product. It is sharp, so save it for a guest who has been genuinely candid.
followups: What would you have changed if the numbers had allowed?
questions.avoid_if: The guest is currently marketing that specific project.

questions.text: What do people blame developers for that is actually a zoning or financing constraint?
questions.lands_because: Lets a developer redirect blame toward structure rather than defend themselves, which produces a far more informative answer about how housing actually gets built.
followups: And what do developers actually deserve blame for?
